H1.title: Lineage-Structured Sequence Novelty vs Divergence and Gene-Content Overlap in Desert Thermoplasmatota
H1.execution_status: COMPLETE (Slurm job 53704703 on IBEX, 00:00:43, exit 0:0; 67/67 SHA-256 checksums verified; full finite census n = 237 dereplicated desert Thermoplasmatota species representatives across 7 PGLS specifications S1-S7 reproduced to <= 5.16e-12 via statsmodels.GLS)
H1.main_vs_supplement: Main text: 2-3 sentences in the Thermoplasmatota subsection (manuscript/main.tex lines 239-279) stating that species-level sequence novelty (f_novel) across the 237 dereplicated Thermoplasmatota species is strongly lineage-structured (Pagel's lambda_ML = 0.9158, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.8463, 0.9578], LRT vs lambda = 0: 2 Delta ell = 229.56, p = 7.44e-52) and that conditional on phylogeny and assembly covariates, proteome-wide AAI (+0.001704 +/- 0.000407, p = 4.07e-5) and reciprocal-best-hit gene-content overlap (-0.137484 +/- 0.019456, p = 1.88e-11) to nearest GTDB/MGnify relatives carry opposite partial associations. Supplement: full 7-model specification table (S1-S7), lambda profile-likelihood curve, comparator sharing diagnostics (32 unique GTDB/MGnify reference MAGs), and dual gene-caller harmonization notes.
supported_claims: Across all n = 237 dereplicated Rub' al-Khali Thermoplasmatota species representatives (185 c__SW-10-69-26, 51 c__E2, 1 c__Thermoplasmata) placed on the 1,914-tip GTDB-Tk r232 ar53 backbone tree, species-level sequence novelty (f_novel) exhibits strong phylogenetic signal under Pagel's lambda PGLS (lambda_ML = 0.915784, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.846303, 0.957823], LRT against OLS lambda = 0: 2 Delta ell = 229.5585, p = 7.44e-52; R^2_GLS = 0.4691).

In the primary PGLS model (S1, df = 230) controlling for CheckM2 completeness (beta = -0.000335 +/- 0.000126, p = 0.0084), contamination (beta = -0.000320 +/- 0.000491, p = 0.5159), log10 genome length (beta = +0.115427 +/- 0.018391, p = 1.71e-9), and log10 N50 (beta = -0.009005 +/- 0.003031, p = 0.00328), f_novel has a positive partial slope on nearest-relative proteome-wide AAI (beta_AAI = +0.001704 +/- 0.000407, t = +4.1847, two-sided p = 4.07e-5, conditional 95% CI [+0.000902, +0.002506], profile-propagated 95% union CI [+0.000836, +0.002534]) and a negative partial slope on RBH orthologous gene-content overlap (beta_RBH = -0.137484 +/- 0.019456, t = -7.0664, two-sided p = 1.88e-11, conditional 95% CI [-0.175819, -0.099149], profile-propagated 95% union CI [-0.176359, -0.095479]).

The opposite-signed partial slopes for AAI and RBH overlap remain directionally and statistically consistent across all six pre-specified sensitivity models (S2 raw counts, S3 logit-transformed f_novel, S4 class-restricted c__SW-10-69-26 n = 185, S5 class-fixed-effects n = 236, S6 within-class comparator-restricted n = 236, and S7 CheckM2-harmonized denominator f_novel_aai n = 232).
prohibited_claims: Do not claim a positive bivariate/marginal correlation between nearest-relative AAI and f_novel (the marginal correlation is negative, Pearson r = -0.088; the positive PGLS slope is strictly a partial regression effect conditional on holding RBH gene-content overlap and genome length constant).
Do not claim that the opposite partial signs of AAI and RBH prove horizontal gene transfer (HGT), de novo gene birth, or adaptive desert specialization.

Do not describe the 32 external reference comparators (25 GTDB r232 and 7 MGnify genomes) as cultivated isolates or type strains; all 32 are uncultured environmental MAGs, and 1 of the 237 pairs (bin_id = 35174, c__Thermoplasmata) is a cross-class match to c__Poseidoniia at 48.68% AAI.

Do not present Student-t confidence intervals and p-values as design-based random-sampling inference over a larger catalog; the 237 genomes are the complete finite cohort of dereplicated Thermoplasmatota species in this study, so intervals are model-based evolutionary superpopulation quantities conditioned on a single fixed FastTree topology.

H2.title: Genomic Neighbourhood Synteny and Flanking KO Conservation Across Multi-Species Structural Dark Families (K vs QnotK)
H2.execution_status: COMPLETE (Slurm job 53738443 on IBEX, 00:05:21, exit 0:0; 26/26 snapshot files and 13/13 result SHA-256 checksums verified; full Gate 3 census of 1,461 multi-species families and 7,604 member rows across 2,126 refined bins audited and reproduced)
H2.main_vs_supplement: Main text: 1-2 sentences in the structural dark proteome subsection (manuscript/main.tex lines 281-319) reporting that among the 353 multi-species families evaluable under complete 4-flank exact-coordinate Bakta windows (30.35% of K, 20.20% of QnotK), both known-fold (K: 40.46% vs 8.71% same-contig positional expectation, p = 0.0002) and novel-fold candidate (QnotK: 32.22% vs 6.56% positional expectation, p = 0.0002) families show strong non-mobilome syntenic conservation, but K and QnotK do not differ once stratified or matched on species breadth, coarse phylum group, and flanking KO annotation density (Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.0354, p = 0.4069; strict 96-pair matched raw difference 0.0000, p = 1.0000). Supplement: full 2,838 -> 1,461 -> 353 (Tier 1) / 637 (Tier 2) / 1,320 (Tier 3) attrition funnel, flank coordinate audit categories, 16-stratum common-support table, caliper matching diagnostics, and multivariable regression tables.
supported_claims: Across the 2,838 confidence-qualified (pLDDT >= 0.70, monomer) structural dark families, 1,461 (51.48%: 570 K, 891 QnotK) span >= 2 distinct dRep 95% ANI species clusters (7,604 member rows; 4,542 primary species-representative loci across 2,126 refined bins, of which 2,041/2,126 = 96.0% are verified by exact uppercase contig SHA-256 and Bakta orig-id with zero hash or reverse-complement mismatches).

Under the primary Tier 1 complete-window gate (>= 2 species with all 4 flanks m2, m1, p1, p2 present on the contig and mapped by exact coordinates to Bakta/eggNOG; n = 353 evaluable families: 173 K, 180 QnotK), recurrent flanking KO synteny is strongly enriched above same-contig eligible-position expectations (B = 5,000 draws) within both K (40.46% [70/173] observed vs 8.71% expected; within-arm excess +31.75 percentage points, p = 0.0002) and QnotK (32.22% [58/180] observed vs 6.56% expected; within-arm excess +25.67 percentage points, p = 0.0002), with zero mobilome/transposase flags among the best recurrent KOs of all 128 recurrent families.

Between arms, K does not exhibit higher neighborhood synteny conservation than QnotK once differences in species breadth, coarse phylum composition, and flanking KO annotation opportunity are controlled: in Tier 1 (n = 353, 16/16 common-support strata, 100% coverage), Mantel-Haenszel stratified difference is Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.0354 (p = 0.4069) and Delta_MH(C_fam) = +0.0489 (p = 0.3204); in Tier 2 (3'-stop match sensitivity, n = 637: 260 K, 377 QnotK), Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.0184 (p = 0.5618) and Delta_MH(C_fam) = +0.0258 (p = 0.5067); in strict 1:1 exact-phylum and tight-length matching (96 pairs, all post-match |SMD| <= 0.130), raw recurrence is 31.25% in both arms (Delta = 0.0000, p = 1.0000) and excess difference is -0.0054 (p = 0.9226); in multivariable OLS/HC3, beta_is_k = +0.0294 +/- 0.0430 (p = 0.4930) on E_fam and +0.0428 +/- 0.0472 (p = 0.3646) on C_fam.
prohibited_claims: Do not claim that known-fold dark families (K) have higher genomic neighborhood conservation than novel-fold candidates (QnotK).

Do not cite the unadjusted Tier 3 partial-window comparison (33.59% vs 24.66%, raw difference +8.93 percentage points, Fisher p = 0.000458 across n = 1,320 families with >= 1 mapped flank) as evidence of a true biological difference between K and QnotK; Tier 3 lacks a same-contig positional null and is confounded by unequal numbers of callable flanks per locus (2.80 in K vs 2.71 in QnotK) and higher species breadth in K (3.22 vs 2.91).

Do not extrapolate Tier 1 neighborhood conservation rates (40.46% in K, 32.22% in QnotK) as unconditional population estimates for all 2,838 structural dark families or all 1,461 multi-species families without stating that 75.84% (1,108/1,461) of Gate 3 families are excluded by contig-edge truncation and coordinate-matching attrition, and that Tier 1 survival is significantly higher in K (30.35%) than in QnotK (20.20%, Fisher p = 1.15e-5).

major_findings.title: Severe and differential complete-window attrition in Tier 1 (30.35% K vs 20.20% QnotK) and unadjusted flank-completeness confounding in Tier 3
major_findings.evidence: reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round7/snapshots/h2_initial/results/pilot_family_conservation.tsv, pilot_neighbourhoods.tsv, and pilot_conservation_summary.json. Only 353/1,461 (24.16%) Gate 3 families pass Tier 1 (173/570 = 30.35% in K vs 180/891 = 20.20% in QnotK, Fisher p = 1.15e-5) because K families have higher baseline species counts (mean 3.30 vs 2.99), longer median contigs (12,608 bp vs 10,256.5 bp), and fewer 5' start shifts (11.2% vs 12.7%). Conversely, Tier 3 (n = 1,320, >= 1 mapped flank) reports only an unadjusted raw difference (+8.93 percentage points, p = 0.000458) without positional expectations or adjustment for unequal callable flanks per locus.
major_findings.concrete_repair: When reporting H2 in the manuscript and Supplement, state the Tier 1 attrition rate (353/1,461 = 24.16%) and arm-specific survival (30.35% K vs 20.20% QnotK) alongside Tier 2 (637/1,461 = 43.60%, where per-locus survival equalizes at 49.73% vs 49.44% and Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.0184, p = 0.5618), and explicitly label Tier 3 as an unadjusted partial-window sensitivity confounded by unequal flank completeness and species breadth.
